Job Summary

Who were looking for: An AI Product Builder who thinks in terms of problems, systems, and leverage and is excited to use AI to turn ideas into working solutions. Youre someone who likes getting your hands dirty, experimenting with new tools, and building and testing solutions quickly, with a strong bias toward action and real-world validation.

What the role is about: At Kraftshala, youll work on problems across student experience, revenue (admissions, sales, marketing), and internal operations. Youll identify opportunities, figure out what to build, and use AI, automation, and modern tools to turn ideas into working products, workflows, and systems. Youll work closely with product and engineering teams to take validated solutions from prototype to production.

What makes this role meaningful: Rather than spending most of your time writing requirements or waiting for development cycles, youll be expected to experiment, prototype, ship, and learn quickly.

Responsibilities

As an AI Product Builder at Kraftshala, youll be at the intersection of product, technology, and business. Youll work closely with teams across the organisation to understand how they work, spot opportunities for improvement, and build solutions that make a meaningful difference.

Youll be expected to move quickly from understanding to experimentation using AI and modern tools to explore different approaches, build prototypes, and learn what works. As solutions take shape, youll work with the right teams to refine, scale, and improve them.

A core expectation in this role is the ability to build quickly and learn through experimentation using AI-assisted development, LLMs, APIs, integrations, automation, and modular systems to turn ideas into usable solutions, validate them in real contexts, and iterate based on what you learn.

What youll own

  • Find Understand Problems: Work with users and teams to identify meaningful problems, understand what causing them, and figure out what is worth solving.
  • Build Prototype: Turn ideas into working prototypes, tools, workflows, and automations using AI and modern development tools. Metrics to measure: Time from idea to prototype, number of experiments shipped
  • Test Iterate: Put what you build in front of real users, learn from feedback and data, and improve the solution based on what you learn. Metrics to measure: Adoption, iteration velocity, solution effectiveness
  • Ship Improve: Work with product and engineering teams to take validated solutions into production and continuously improve them based on usage and impact. Metrics to measure: Delivery speed, adoption, business impact

How youll operate

  • You move fluidly between understanding the problem and building the solution
  • You use AI as a force multiplier across research, prototyping, development, and execution
  • You default to building and testing, rather than spending too long planning
  • Youre comfortable trying things that may not work and iterating quickly
  • You prioritise speed to insight and usable output over perfect upfront planning
  • You think in systems, not just features
  • You care about what happens after something is built adoption, impact, and outcomes

Monthly Outcomes

  • Month 1: Build a strong understanding of Kraftshala users, systems, and business priorities
  • Month 1: Identify and validate meaningful problems worth solving
  • Month 1: Build and ship at least one small prototype, automation, or workflow improvement
  • Month 2: Own a problem from understanding to solution
  • Month 2: Build, test, and iterate on prototypes using AI and modern tools
  • Month 2: Ship at least one meaningful product, workflow, or automation improvement
  • Month 3+: Take on increasingly complex problems and build solutions with greater autonomy
  • Month 3+: Run faster build-test-learn cycles and improve what you ship based on real-world feedback
  • Month 3+: Deliver solutions that create measurable improvements in user experience, revenue, or operational efficiency

Must Haves

  • 12 years of experience in Product, a builder, technical, or closely related role startup experience is a plus. (Were not fussed about the exact years of experience, as that just a proxy for your skill level.)
  • Have built and shipped something a digital product, tool, prototype, workflow, automation, or similar.
  • Hands-on experience with AI-assisted development, APIs, automation, no-code/low-code, or modern development tools.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and a bias for action.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-moving contexts.
  • Strong user empathy, product intuition, and communication skills.

Job Summary

Within the Digital Customer Relationship organization, you are responsible for defining how Artificial Intelligence can be leveraged within your capability scope to answer business needs while ensuring coherence, scalability, maintainability and alignment with enterprise standards. You act as the AI solution authority for your capability. You help translate validated business requirements into AI-enabled solution options and formal recommendation papers, covering AI embedded in existing platforms, vendor capabilities, low-code / pro-code developments, autonomous agents and AI-native platforms. Your mission is to ensure that the right AI solution pattern is selected and designed before delivery starts. You work closely with Business Product Leaders, Business Process Owners, E2E Business Architects, Digital Product Owners, Application Analysts, E2E Solution Design Leads, DCR Architects, Technical Leads, AI Hub, Data Office, platform owners and delivery teams. You do not replace the Business Product Leader, the Digital Product Owner, the E2E Solution Design Lead or the Technical Lead. You complement them by bringing AI-specific architecture, assessment and design expertise into the existing Services Ways of Working. Your impact will be measured by the quality of AI solution decisions, the reuse of scalable patterns, the clarity of architecture recommendations, and the ability of delivered AI solutions to move safely into run mode.

Responsibilities

  • AI Opportunity and Feasibility Assessment: Analyze validated business requirements and identify whether AI can bring a relevant, measurable and feasible answer to the business need. Support early discovery and handover discussions by clarifying AI opportunities, constraints, prerequisites and risks. Assess data readiness, process readiness, platform readiness and operational readiness before recommending an AI solution path. Challenge solution assumptions where AI is not the right answer, or where a simpler non-AI solution could deliver sufficient business value.
  • AI Solution Option Assessment: Prepare structured AI assessment papers comparing the relevant solution options: embedded AI in existing platforms, vendor AI capability, low-code AI, pro-code AI, autonomous agents, AI-native platforms and reuse of existing AI assets. Evaluate each option against business fit, user experience, technical feasibility, integration impact, data needs, cybersecurity, compliance, cost, scalability, maintainability and run complexity. Document clear recommendations, assumptions, trade-offs and decision points to support build-versus-buy decisions at Services Digital Experience or DCR leadership level.
  • AI Solution Design: Define the AI solution pattern within the capability scope, including where the intelligence is executed, which platforms are impacted, how users interact with the solution, and how decisions or actions are controlled. Design AI interaction patterns, agent flows, human-in-the-loop mechanisms, fallback scenarios, knowledge sources, data flows, integration points and monitoring requirements. Ensure the AI design is consistent with existing E2E solution flows, application responsibilities, architectural standards and target business architecture. Contribute to Functional and Technical Design Documents by providing AI-specific architecture input, assumptions, constraints and non-functional requirements.
  • Architecture Alignment and Governance: Collaborate with the Global AI Architect, AI Hub, DCR Architects, Data Office, cybersecurity and platform owners to ensure compliance with enterprise AI principles and guardrails. Participate in the AI Architecture Board and other governance forums for complex, strategic or cross-platform initiatives. Promote reuse of approved AI patterns, agent frameworks, connectors, data patterns, monitoring approaches and integration standards.
  • Delivery Support and Technical Decision Enablement: Support Digital Product Owners, Application Analysts, E2E Solution Design Leads, Technical Leads and delivery teams during backlog definition, solution scoping and implementation preparation. Clarify AI architecture choices, constraints, prerequisites, dependencies and risks during delivery planning and execution. Support issue resolution when AI behavior, data dependencies, model outputs, integrations or agent flows create delivery or quality risks.
  • AI Run, Monitoring and Support Readiness: Define AI-specific run requirements before go-live, including AI agent ownership, prompt / configuration ownership, knowledge source ownership, monitoring needs, escalation paths and support levels. Ensure AI agents and AI-enabled solutions are designed with observability, traceability, quality monitoring, feedback loops and continuous improvement routines. Support transition to run by ensuring documentation, operating procedures, known limitations and ownership models are explicit and accepted.

Requirements

  • Master degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Digital Technologies or equivalent experience.
  • 8-12+ years in architecture, software engineering, platform engineering, solution design or digital transformation roles.
  • Experience designing enterprise solutions involving multiple applications, integrations, data flows and non-functional constraints.
  • Practical understanding of AI technologies such as copilots, embedded AI, RAG, AI agents, workflow automation, low-code / pro-code AI developments and AI observability.

Skills and Competencies

  • Strong architecture and system design mindset, with the ability to translate business problems into pragmatic AI solution patterns.
  • Strong analytical capability to compare options, expose trade-offs and make fact-based recommendations.
  • Ability to simplify complex AI concepts for business, product and delivery stakeholders.
  • Good understanding of data, integration, cybersecurity, user experience and run implications of AI solutions.
  • Curious, pragmatic and continuously learning about emerging AI technologies and platform vendor capabilities.
  • Strong documentation and presentation skills, especially for assessment papers and architecture decision records.
  • Ability to influence without formal authority and work effectively in a matrix organization.
  • Success measures AI solution assessments are complete, structured and useful for decision-making.
  • Recommended AI solution patterns are scalable, maintainable, secure and aligned with enterprise guardrails.
  • Build-versus-buy decisions are supported by clear trade-offs and documented rationale.
  • Capabilities reuse common AI patterns instead of creating fragmented solutions.
  • AI solutions have clear data, integration, monitoring, ownership and run models before go-live.
  • Delivery teams receive timely and actionable architecture guidance for AI initiatives.

jobDescription:
PLAYER-COACH TALENT ACQUISITION

LEAD

Talent Acquisition & HR Mentoring | Bengaluru | Hybrid

About the Role

Zenskar is in hyper-growth mode, scaling past 100+ full-time employees across India and the US. We are building an

A-lister team and scalable people processesnot just solving the next few hires.

We are looking for a Player-Coach Talent Acquisition leader who can own talent acquisition end-to-end while helping

shape the HR side of the function as it grows. This role is approximately 80% Talent Acquisition and 20% HR

mentoring/support. You will lead a team of 3 across TA/HR and interns while remaining hands-on as an IC recruiter.

What You’ll Own

Talent Acquisition (~80%)

  • Sourcing & Pipeline: Build and run sourcing strategies for open roles and maintain strong pipelines so hiring managers

are never waiting.

  • Co-founder & Hiring Manager Partnership: Sharpen JDs, run intake calls, and drive timely, clear feedback from hiring

managers.

  • Candidate Experience: Own a fast, structured and respectful process from first outreach through offer.
  • Agency & Vendor Coordination: Manage external recruiting agencies where required, including US hiring, and hold

them accountable for quality and turnaround.

  • Reporting & Process: Track pipeline health, time-to-fill and source effectiveness; identify bottlenecks before they

become escalations.

  • Onboarding Handoff: Partner with Ops/Admin to ensure a smooth transition from offer acceptance to onboarding.

HR Mentoring & Support (~20%)

  • Mentor the HR team as a sounding board for judgment calls, escalations and unfamiliar situations.
  • Help shape performance frameworks, policies and processes without owning day-to-day HR execution.
  • Connect TA and HR by bringing market insights, compensation benchmarks, candidate expectations and attrition

signals into HR frameworks.

What This Role Is

  • A doer’s seat: You will source, screen and close candidates yourself—not just manage a dashboard.
  • Coach & Manage: Manage TA/HR team members and their outcomes.
  • Built for Range: Move between closing candidates, advising on HR frameworks and coaching teammates in the same

week.

  • Growth Track: A natural path toward a broader TA/HR leadership role as the company and function scale.

Best Fit

  • 9–12 years of experience in Talent Acquisition, with genuine curiosity or prior exposure to HR/HRBP work.
  • Comfortable owning full-cycle recruiting independently—from sourcing through offer—without heavy hand-holding.
  • Experience managing a team of 2+ people across TA/HR.
  • Startup experience preferred; comfortable with ambiguity and building processes rather than inheriting them.
  • Prior experience at a high-growth Series A–D B2B AI/SaaS company where you helped scale the TA motion during a

growth phase.

  • Experience seeing headcount scale from approximately 80 employees to 300+.
  • Direct, plain communicator with candidates, hiring managers, agencies and the HR team.
  • Experience hiring US roles from India is a strong plus, given the market gap and complexity of running this market solo.

Location & Work Model

Work Model Hybrid — 2 days per week (Tuesday & Thursday)



Ideal Candidate Profile: A hands-on TA leader who can independently close critical hires, build scalable recruiting

systems, manage and coach a small team, partner confidently with founders and hiring managers, and bring practical

market insight into HR decision-making.

Detailed JD:

**Role Summary**

The Lead, Data Quality & Responsible AI Control Operations is a senior hands-on lead responsible for defining, operationalizing, and continuously improving enterprise data quality and AI data readiness controls across authorized data sources, data products, and AI use cases. This role bridges data architecture, hands-on data modeling, data management, Responsible AI, and control operations to ensure AI products consume governed, traceable, fit-for-purpose, and high-quality data. The ideal candidate brings strong practical experience in data quality engineering, data architecture, data modeling, data governance, metadata, lineage, control design, and automation, with the ability to lead domain adoption and influence business, technology, risk, privacy, compliance, audit, and AI governance stakeholders.

**Team Context**

This role sits at the intersection of Data Management & Governance, enterprise data quality assurance, Responsible AI operations, data architecture, and technology risk management. The position is accountable for making quality and governance requirements executable in the flow of delivery by embedding controls into data sourcing, ADS and data product certification, metadata and lineage workflows, pipeline validation, AI lifecycle gates, monitoring, exception management, remediation, recertification, and evidence generation. The role will help mature a control plane that provides visibility into AI data readiness, data quality health, control coverage, exceptions, incidents, remediation status, and audit-ready evidence.

## Key Responsibilities

  •        Lead enterprise implementation of data quality and AI data readiness controls across authorized data sources, data products, semantic products, and AI use cases.
  •        Define what AI-ready data means in practice, including quality thresholds, lineage completeness, metadata completeness, source authorization, classification, access controls, issue history, freshness, and remediation expectations.
  •        Translate Responsible AI control requirements into measurable data control requirements that can be embedded into data pipelines, certification workflows, metadata platforms, dashboards, and evidence routines.
  •        Partner with data architects, data engineering, platform, and domain teams to determine where controls belong across ingestion, transformation, publication, semantic access, AI consumption, and runtime monitoring.
  •        Perform hands-on data modeling across conceptual, logical, physical, canonical, and semantic models to support trusted data products, ADS certification, AI consumption patterns, and downstream DQ control design.
  •        Define reusable DQ and RAI control patterns, rule templates, evidence payloads, operating routines, and implementation guidance that domain teams can adopt consistently.
  •        Guide domain teams on defining DQ rules, setting thresholds, emitting raw DQ metrics, managing exceptions, remediating issues, and providing evidence without duplicating central governance processes.
  •        Establish operating routines for recurring data profiling, rule execution, exception review, issue triage, root-cause analysis, remediation tracking, retesting, recertification, and closure evidence.
  •        Integrate data quality controls into AI lifecycle gates so AI products use fit-for-purpose, authorized, governed, traceable, and appropriately controlled data sources.
  •        Define and maintain control libraries for data quality, AI data readiness, metadata, lineage, access, privacy, monitoring, certification, and lifecycle governance.
  •        Drive automation opportunities that reduce manual governance burden while improving traceability, repeatability, defensibility, and audit readiness.
  •        Define monitoring thresholds, alerts, KRIs, KPIs, control effectiveness measures, and reporting routines that provide senior leaders visibility into data quality health, AI data readiness, exceptions, and remediation progress.
  •        Coordinate across business owners, product teams, data domains, platform engineering, architecture, security, privacy, legal, compliance, risk, model risk, and audit to ensure consistent execution of control requirements.
  •        Maintain audit-ready documentation, including control mappings, rule logic, test results, workflow decisions, approvals, exceptions, incident records, remediation evidence, and management reporting.
  •        Lead playbooks, standards, implementation guidance, training, and enablement materials that help business and technology teams adopt DQ and RAI control practices at scale.

## Required Skills and Experience

  •        Strong experience in enterprise data quality, data governance, data management, data architecture, technology controls, Responsible AI operations, or a closely related discipline within a complex enterprise environment.
  •        Strong understanding of enterprise data architecture, hands-on data modeling, authorized data sources, data products, data contracts, metadata, lineage, semantic layers, access controls, and governed lakehouse or cloud data platform patterns.
  •        Hands-on experience designing and reviewing conceptual, logical, physical, canonical, dimensional, domain, and semantic data models, including entity relationships, critical data elements, business definitions, data contracts, and AI-consumable semantic structures.
  •        Hands-on knowledge of data quality frameworks, including rule design, profiling, thresholds, data observability, reconciliation, anomaly detection, issue management, remediation, and quality scorecards.
  •        Ability to connect data quality outcomes to Responsible AI control needs, including traceability, data suitability, representativeness, bias/proxy-risk considerations, privacy constraints, monitoring, and lifecycle governance.
  •        Experience embedding controls into pipelines, workflows, platforms, certification routines, metadata systems, or CI/CD processes rather than relying solely on manual review.
  •        Familiarity with AI/ML, generative AI, agentic AI, model lifecycle management, model registries, evaluation workflows, monitoring, and production release controls.
  •        Ability to map policy, regulatory, and control expectations into practical requirements, acceptance criteria, testing procedures, operating routines, and evidence expectations.
  •        Experience working with cross-functional control partners such as risk, compliance, legal, privacy, information security, model risk, internal audit, and business control teams.
  •        Ability to define metrics and dashboards that communicate control coverage, control effectiveness, exceptions, incidents, data quality health, AI data readiness, and remediation progress.
  •        Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical and governance concepts into clear guidance for executives, practitioners, and control partners.
  •        Strong execution and leadership skills, including backlog management, stakeholder alignment, decision documentation, operating model design, issue tracking, and delivery against milestones.

## Preferred Qualifications

  •        Experience in a regulated industry such as financial services, insurance, healthcare, or another environment with strong risk, privacy, security, and audit expectations.
  •        Experience with Data Quality, Responsible AI, AI governance, data governance, model risk management, technology risk, or operational risk frameworks.
  •        Working knowledge of data quality and observability tools, metadata/catalog platforms, lineage tooling, workflow tools, cloud platforms, issue management systems, and reporting/dashboarding tools.
  •        Experience designing DQ rule libraries, control catalogs, evidence schemas, certification criteria, policy

As part of our EY GDS-ServiceNow team, you will work to solve client problems using ServiceNow platform. You will get an opportunity to work with high quality team. You will get an opportunity to build innovating product which solves client s problem.

The opportunity

We re looking for Lead Architect with expertise in ServiceNow Implementation and specifically Moveworks AI to join the EYD GDS ServiceNow. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of a leading firm whilst being instrumental in the growth.

The architect designs and owns the AI front door experience for employees, where Moveworks acts as the primary conversational layer over ServiceNow processes.

Key focus areas

  • Performs Configuration/Customization of the ServiceNow system, including creation workflows
  • Architecting end-to-end AI agents that combine:
    • Moveworks Reasoning Engine
    • ServiceNow workflows, approvals, and policies
  • Defining when the AI resolves fully vs. hands off to human agents
  • Designing reusable agent patterns (HR)
  • Performs integrations and process automation using Orchestration, Web Services, Soap calls, etc.
  • Load, manipulate and maintain data between ServiceNow and other systems as needed
  • Gathers specifications from the business departments and delivers a product/release that meets the needs presented. Interprets business and functional requirements and develops technical specifications documentation
  • Work with business liaison to generate dashboards, home pages, performance analytics data collectors and reports as needed
  • Must analyse and fully understand user stories and internal procedures to improve system capabilities, automate process workflows and address scheduling limitations throughout the development and delivery of the ServiceNow releases
  • Own Architectural reviews, quality reviews and technical documentation
  • Performs system and integration testing with sample and live data

Skills and attributes for success

  • Deep understanding of Moveworks AI Assistant Enterprise Search
  • Experience designing conversational flows that replace portals/forms
  • -Hands-on experience with Moveworks-ServiceNow integration architecture
  • Authentication protocols such as IAM/Active Directory / LDAP or SiteMinder federation /Azure
  • Integrating with internal and external applications and systems
  • JavaScript, HTML, Angular JS and good web design practices
  • Implementation experience on any of the following applications on ITSM, HRSD, Service Portal, Agentic AI, Gen AI.
  • Disciplined Agile Delivery software release build/deploy processes

To qualify for the role, you must have

  • College degree in related technology field (Computer, Engineering, Science, etc.) or comparable job experiences
  • Approximately 10+ years of experience in a development role. Able to exhibit a progression of increasingly complex job responsibilities during the period
  • ServiceNow CSA certification is mandatory, CIS-HRSD is favourable

Ideally, you ll also have

  • Experience on SDLC or TFS or JIRA or equivalent tool to maintain stories.
  • Knowledge about ServiceNow s latest version s features.

What we look for

  • A Team of people with commercial acumen, technical experience and enthusiasm to learn new things in this fast-moving environment
  • An opportunity to be a part of market-leading, multi-disciplinary team of 1000+ professionals, in the only integrated global transaction business worldwide.
  • Opportunities to work with EY ServiceNow practices globally with leading businesses across a range of industries

What working at EY offers

At EY, we re dedicated to helping our clients, from start-ups to Fortune 500 companies - and the work we do with them is as varied as they are.

You get to work with inspiring and meaningful projects. Our focus is education and coaching alongside practical experience to ensure your personal development. We value our employees and you will be able to control your own development with an individual progression plan. You will quickly grow into a responsible role with challenging and stimulating assignments. Moreover, you will be part of an interdisciplinary environment that emphasizes high quality and knowledge exchange. Plus, we offer:

  • Support, coaching and feedback from some of the most engaging colleagues around
  • Opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
  • The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that s right for you

EY | Building a better working world

Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.

The Principal Architect is the design authority for this entire customer-facing digital estate and leads a group of 4-5 Technical Architects spanning AEM and content platforms, frontend frameworks, cloud and platform engineering, and AI and data. The role is deliberately multi-stack: it is accountable for a single coherent North-star architecture across content, experience, services, cloud and intelligence layers, rather than for the depth of any one stack. Deep, demonstrable AI engineering capability is a mandatory requirement of the role - the Principal Architect defines how LLM, agentic and evaluation-driven systems are architected, governed and run inside a regulated NBFC.   • Ensure architecture, decision records and runbooks are documented, current and usable, so that platform knowledge does not sit only with individuals.
  • 5. Leadership and Team Development: Lead, coach and grow 2-4 Technical Architects - set objectives, conduct reviews, close appraisal cycles on time, and build a genuine succession bench for each stack.
  • Deliberately build cross-stack breadth in the architect group so that the organisation is not exposed to single-person dependency in any technology area.

  • Determine individual training and development plans, sponsor certification and conference participation, and create visible technical career paths for engineers below the architect band.

  • Keep delivery activity firmly connected to business outcomes, working with cross-functional teams on acquisition, conversion and cross-sell targets.
  • 6. Risk, Compliance and Commercial Governance: Own the architecture-level risk posture for the estate covering information security, data privacy and localisation, third-party and supply chain risk, and regulatory obligations applicable to an RBI-regulated NBFC.
  • Partner with Information Security, Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit as the technical counterpart on reviews, findings and remediation, and represent the platform architecture in regulatory and audit engagements.

descriptionFromApi:
Who are we
Equinix is the worlds digital infrastructure company, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.
A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.
Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriersbecause progress starts with fresh ideas. Youll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes youbecause when you feel valued, youre empowered to do your best work.
Job Summary
Equinix Incubation builds the agentic systems that run the software delivery lifecycle end to end: a fleet of specialized AI agents, with humans directing the work and owning every gate. Someone has to own the product, the roadmap, and the team behind it. That is this role.
You will lead the engineering pods that build the orchestration layer, the persona consoles, and the agents themselves, and carry the roadmap from first MVP to organization-wide scale. This is a player-coach role for a leader who can hold a product vision, an architecture, an executive audience, and a hiring plan in their head at the same time.
Responsibilities
Own the Product and the Roadmap
  • Define and drive the delivery-engine roadmap: orchestrator, agent fleet, consoles, dashboards, and enterprise integrations, sequenced for value
  • Make the build-measure-learn loop real: ship in sprints, pilot with live delivery teams, and let adoption and telemetry reshape the plan
  • Own trade-off decisions across scope, quality, cost, and speed, and defend them with data in front of senior leadership
Build and Lead the Pods
  • Hire, grow, and retain a small, exceptional team of agent engineers, platform engineers, and delivery talent across the UK and India
  • Run lean pods where agents do the routine work and people do the judgment work; model that way of working yourself
  • Set a high, kind bar: clear expectations, honest feedback, and career growth in the most modern engineering discipline there is
Prove the Value
  • Own the value story: cycle time, throughput, quality, adoption, and realized business value, instrumented and reported without drama
  • Keep the economics honest: agent cost, platform cost, and capacity unlocked, treated as first-class engineering metrics
  • Turn pilot wins into an expansion case that finance and function leaders believe
Set the Operating Standard
  • Establish how agent-first engineering is done: evals as release gates, human-in-the-loop approvals, and responsible AI governance with InfoSec and the AI council
  • Represent the platform in architecture and governance forums, and keep the roadmap aligned with enterprise platform and data strategy
  • Share patterns, standards, and playbooks so other teams can adopt what your team proves
What Success Looks Like
  • The delivery engine is in daily use by live delivery teams, with measurable cycle-time and quality gains that survive finance scrutiny
  • You have built a team people want to join, with a hiring record and retention that show it
  • Executives trust your roadmap because what you commit to ships, and what ships gets measured
  • The operating standards your team set are being adopted beyond your team
Qualifications
  • 12+ years in software engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams or engineering-led products
  • A record of shipping and scaling platforms or products in an enterprise, from first release through adoption
  • Hands-on fluency with modern AI: LLM-powered applications, agentic systems, and what it takes to make them production-grade
  • Strong architectural judgment across APIs, event-driven systems, cloud platforms, and enterprise integration
  • Proven hiring and talent development record, including building distributed teams
  • Executive-grade communication: you can carry a room of senior stakeholders with a clear, honest narrative
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience delivering AI or automation platforms into regulated or security-conscious enterprises
  • Experience with agent frameworks and protocols such as MCP or A2A, and with eval-driven quality practices
  • Experience running product operating models: roadmaps, funding cases, value realization
  • Background in developer platforms, SDLC tooling, or engineering productivity
Core Competencies
Product Technical Leadership
  • Roadmap ownership; architectural judgment; trade-off decision-making; systems thinking
People Leadership
  • Hiring and talent development; lean pod design; coaching; distributed team leadership
AI-First Operating Model
  • Agent-first ways of working; evals and governance; human-in-the-loop design; value instrumentation
Executive Influence
  • Narrative and communication; stakeholder alignment; funding and value cases; calm under scrutiny
Why This Role
Incubation is a durable capability, not a project team: the team persists, and the product rotates. Agentic delivery is product one; the next incubation bets follow. You will define how AI-first engineering works at Equinix and build the team that proves it. Few director roles come with a mandate this clear and a canvas this open.

Core Engineering builds the firmware and cloud platform that Plumes next-generation architecture is built on. We deliver the Plume Firmware Agent (PFA) across three reference platforms - RDK-B , prplOS / prplMesh , and OpenWRT / OpenSync - The highly scalable cloud core manages a fleet of connected devices over standards-based protocols.

About the role
Were hiring an Engineering Manager to lead one of Core Engineerings delivery teams. This is a hands-on-adjacent people-leadership role: you own the health, growth and output of a team of roughly 10-30 firmware, backend and QA engineers, and you are close enough to the technology to make real calls on scope, sequencing and trade-offs.

  • Track and unblock cross-team dependencies with Product Engineering, Integration Engineering, Cloud/CSS, DevOps and InfoSec.
Own technical direction with your leads
  • Partner with technical leads and architects on platform strategy - the move from a stateful, driver-coupled OpenSync design toward stateless, standards-compliant, SDK-conformant operation over USP.
  • Make and defend architectural trade-offs across three device platforms and the cloud services above them, including what gets upstreamed versus carried downstream.
  • Raise the engineering bar on the things that quietly decide velocity: build times, branch hygiene, test automation, flaky testbeds, and observability.
What were looking for:
Leadership Skills
  • 13+ years in software engineering with 3+ years managing engineers directly, including hiring and performance management.
  • Strong technical grounding in embedded Linux networking - Wi-Fi/networking firmware, an embedded build system (Yocto/OpenWrt/OpenEmbedded), C, and debugging on real hardware - or in distributed cloud services with genuine fluency in the device side.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a release train: you have shipped firmware or platform software into production at scale; with QA and release gates you were accountable for.
  • Experience leading a distributed team across time zones , and the operating discipline that requires - written communication, asynchronous decision-making, and deliberate inclusion of remote colleagues.
  • Comfort operating in a matrixed organisation with technical leads, TPMs and product owners you influence but dont manage.
Technical Skills
  • Direct experience with one or more of RDK-B , prplOS/prplMesh , or OpenSync/OpenWrt .
  • Working knowledge of Broadband Forum TR-369 (USP) and TR-181 , and/or Wi-Fi Alliance EasyMesh .
  • Background in the CPE / broadband gateway ecosystem - ODM and chipset vendor SDKs, operator certification, interop testing.
  • Familiarity with the surrounding toolchain: Jenkins, GitHub-based workflows, Artifactory, containerised services, Kubernetes/EKS, MQTT, PKI and certificate management.
  • Experience with test automation for embedded systems (e.g. Boardfarm, TDK, cloudless test harnesses) and with managing QA as a first-class discipline rather than an afterthought.
  • Exposure to Wi-Fi 6/6E/7, MLO, and mesh performance work.
About Plume
As the creator of the only open, hardware-independent, cloud-controlled experience platform for ISPs and their subscribers, Plume partners with over 400 ISP customers, including some of the world s largest such as Comcast, Charter, Liberty Global, and J:COM.
Using OpenSync, the most widely supported open-source, silicon-to-cloud framework for smart spaces, Plume s software-defined network allows ISPs to decouple their service offerings from hardware and rapidly curate and deliver new services over a multi-vendor, open-platform architecture.

Job Summary

The International Solar Alliance (ISA) is strengthening its knowledge, learning and capacity-building ecosystem with the ambition to democratize access to high-quality solar knowledge, making relevant knowledge, skills and learning opportunities more accessible to Member Countries, practitioners and other stakeholders globally.

As part of this ambition, ISA aims to establish itself as a leading global reference for solar knowledge and learning, with the aspiration for its digital knowledge ecosystem to become one of the most widely accessed platforms for solar knowledge globally.

Central to this effort is the development of an integrated ISA knowledge and capacity-building ecosystem, bringing together the ISA Academy, STAR-C network, fellowship and training programmes, knowledge products, institutional and academic partnerships, and other relevant initiatives and services. Digital technologies and Artificial Intelligence (AI) will serve as key enablers across this ecosystem, helping ISA improve access to knowledge, personalize learning experiences, facilitate multilingual access, connect knowledge and expertise across countries and institutions, and increase the reach and impact of its knowledge and capacity-building activities.

ISA therefore seeks an AI - Digital Specialist within KMID to support the functional development and application of AI and digital solutions across ISA, with particular focus on knowledge management, learning, capacity building and related digital products and services.

The position will work across ISA units and in close coordination with relevant teams, including IT, as well as external partners, ensuring that digital and AI solutions respond to institutional, programme and user needs while remaining aligned with ISAs technical, security and data requirements.

Objective

The objective of the position is to strengthen ISAs ability to use AI and digital technologies as enablers of knowledge, learning and capacity building.

The Specialist will translate programme, knowledge and user requirements into effective digital solutions; support the development and evolution of ISAs digital knowledge and learning products and services; and facilitate the responsible adoption of AI to improve how ISA creates, organizes, delivers and makes knowledge accessible to Member Countries and other stakeholders.

The role combines functional digital leadership, product development, AI enablement, innovation and project coordination, supported by sufficient technical expertise to assess solutions, guide implementation and effectively engage with technology teams and providers, rather than assuming responsibility for ISAs core IT infrastructure.

Your Role and Scope of work

3.1 Digital Learning and Knowledge Ecosystem

  • Provide functional and digital expertise for the continued development of the ISA Academy and other digital knowledge and learning services.
  • Support the digital enablement and integration of ISAs broader knowledge and capacity-building ecosystem, including STAR-C, fellowships, training programmes, knowledge products and other relevant initiatives.
  • Translate learning, programme and user needs into functional requirements and effective digital solutions.
  • Support AI-enabled functionalities, including personalized learning, multilingual access, intelligent knowledge discovery and other innovative approaches.
  • Use user feedback, data and analytics to continuously improve digital knowledge and learning services and their reach.

3.2 AI and Digital Innovation

  • Identify, develop and support practical applications of AI across ISAs knowledge, learning and capacity-building activities.
  • Explore and prototype AI-enabled solutions that improve access to solar knowledge, technical resources, training content and institutional knowledge.
  • Identify opportunities for digitalization, automation and AI-enabled workflows that strengthen programme delivery and institutional effectiveness.
  • Contribute to the digital and AI dimensions of the Global Capability Centre (GCC), ISA Academy and other ISA initiatives where relevant to knowledge, learning and capacity building.
  • Monitor emerging AI and digital technologies and assess their potential application to ISAs programmes and services.
  • Promote responsible and appropriate use of AI in coordination with relevant ISA functions.

3.3 Digital Products and Project Delivery

  • Support the functional design and continuous improvement of ISAs digital knowledge, learning and capacity-building products and services.
  • Develop functional requirements, product roadmaps, implementation plans and delivery priorities.
  • Coordinate digital initiatives with relevant ISA units, technology providers, consultants, vendors and implementation partners.
  • Monitor deliverables, timelines, quality, testing and user acceptance.
  • Support functional and technical assessment of proposed solutions and vendor deliverables.
  • Promote appropriate integration and information flows between relevant platforms and ISA systems, working with IT and other relevant teams on technical architecture, cybersecurity, hosting, data protection and related requirements.

3.4 Partnerships, Stakeholder Engagement and Representation

  • Support partnerships with governments, technology organizations, academic institutions, development partners, research institutions and other stakeholders in AI, digital learning and knowledge innovation.
  • Identify opportunities to bring external expertise, technologies, content and innovation into ISAs knowledge and capacity-building ecosystem.
  • Engage with ISA Member Countries and partners to understand their needs and promote the adoption and use of relevant digital knowledge and learning solutions.
  • Represent ISA/KMID, as required, in meetings, workshops, conferences and other national and international engagements, presenting ISAs work and contributing to discussions on AI, digital learning, knowledge and capacity building.
  • Support and, where appropriate, lead or facilitate sessions, workshops and knowledge events related to the areas of responsibility.
  • Communicate digital and AI concepts effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior officials, Member Country representatives and institutional partners.

3.5 Cross-ISA Coordination and Quality

  • Work across ISA units to identify opportunities where AI and digital solutions can strengthen knowledge, learning and capacity-building activities.
  • Serve as a functional interface between institutional and programme requirements and relevant technical teams.
  • Support appropriate data governance, responsible AI, accessibility and compliance with ISA policies and standards.
  • Contribute to positioning ISA as an innovative global platform for solar knowledge, learning and capacity building.

Expected Results

  • The AI Digital Specialist will contribute to continued development and enhancement of the ISA digital knowledge and capacity-building ecosystem, including the ISA Academy and relevant AI-enabled capabilities.

  • Excellent communication skills and experience mentoring other engineers

About 100ms
100ms is building AI agents that automate complex patient access workflows in U.S. healthcare - starting with benefits verification, prior authorisation, and referral intake in speciality pharmacy.
Our platform combines LLM-based agents, deep healthcare domain expertise, and operational infrastructure to help care teams move faster and get patients on treatment sooner.
Role Summary
We are looking for a Software Engineer Architect to own the technical architecture of our AI agents platform as it scales. In healthcare, accuracy and trust are everything - our systems make phone calls to payers, handle Protected Health Information, and operate inside real clinical workflows, so the architecture underneath them has to be reliable, observable, secure, and fast to evolve.

This is a hands-on, deeply technical role, not a pure design-review position.
You will define how our services, data, and agent pipelines fit together; make the build-vs-buy and technology choices that shape the next three years of the platform; write code on the hardest problems; and raise the engineering bar across the team.

You will work directly with the founders, product, platform/infrastructure, and security teams, and your decisions will be informed by real customer and clinical workflows.
Key Responsibilities
  1. Own the end-to-end architecture of the AI agents platform - services, APIs, data models, async task pipelines, LLM/voice agent orchestration, and integrations with payer systems, EMRs, and telephony.
  2. Design for reliability, latency, and safety: define patterns for fault tolerance, idempotency, retries, observability, and graceful degradation across agent workflows that run at scale in production.
  3. Set the architecture for multi-tenancy, data isolation, and PHI handling in partnership with our Security and Compliance Lead, keeping HIPAA and SOC 2 requirements designed in rather than bolted on.
  4. Make and document high-leverage technical decisions - build vs. buy, service boundaries, storage and queueing choices, LLM provider and inference strategy - through lightweight design reviews and ADRs.
  5. Stay hands-on: prototype critical paths, write production code on the most ambiguous and highest-risk problems, and unblock teams when they hit hard technical walls.
  6. Partner with the platform team on how workloads run on our Kubernetes (GKE) infrastructure - autoscaling, deployment topology, cost, and SLOs for agent and voice workloads.
  7. Raise the engineering bar: mentor senior engineers, drive code and design review culture, and define standards for testing, evaluation, and release safety across teams.
  8. Translate product and customer needs into a technical roadmap; work with founders and product to sequence architectural investments against business priorities.
  9. De-risk scale: anticipate where the system breaks at 10x call volume, 10x customers, and 10x team size, and lay the groundwork before it does.
Requirements
  1. 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, including several years designing and operating large-scale, production distributed systems.
  2. A track record of owning architecture for a product or platform end to end - you have made foundational technical decisions, lived with their consequences, and evolved them.
  3. Deep expertise in backend systems: service design, RESTful/async APIs, event-driven architectures, task queues, and data modelling across relational and non-relational stores.
  4. Strong grasp of reliability engineering - observability, fault tolerance, capacity planning, and incident-informed design - for systems with strict correctness and latency requirements.
  5. Hands-on proficiency in at least one of our core languages (Python or Go); comfort reading and reviewing code across the stack, including React-based frontends.
  6. Working knowledge of cloud-native infrastructure (GCP/AWS/Azure), Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code, and how architectural choices play out operationally.
  7. Experience building or integrating AI/LLM-backed systems - or clear evidence you can go deep fast on agent orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, and inference trade-offs.
  8. Strong security instincts: you design with data isolation, encryption, access control, and auditability in mind from day one.
  9. Excellent written and verbal communication - you can carry a design from whiteboard to ADR to aligned teams, and explain trade-offs to founders and customers alike.
  10. Ability to tackle complex, ambiguous technical problems and drive them to crisp decisions.
Nice-to-Haves
  1. Experience with voice AI, telephony (SIP/WebRTC), or real-time systems.
  2. Prior work in U.S. healthcare or other regulated domains (HIPAA, SOC 2, HITRUST) - familiarity with EMRs, payer integrations, FHIR/HL7.
  3. Experience with LLM evaluation frameworks, prompt/fine-tuning pipelines, and hallucination/safety controls in production.
  4. Experience scaling engineering teams and architecture together - platformization, service extraction, developer experience.
  5. Open-source contributions, technical writing, or conference talks.
Why This Role Matters
Every architectural decision here has a direct line to patients getting care faster.
The systems you design will determine whether our agents can be trusted with clinical workflows at enterprise scale - and whether a small, sharp team can keep shipping quickly as the platform grows.
You will set technical direction at the stage where it compounds the most.

jobDescription:

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

Job Description
Job Summary:
Software Development Engineers are expert problem-solvers and builders who design, implement, and improve software applications and systems. In this role, engineers spend approximately 6075% of their time coding, working hands-on with code, data, and modern tools (including AI-assisted development, cloud services, and automation frameworks) to deliver secure, scalable, and high-quality technology solutions that drive business outcomes in the fintech sector. They collaborate with cross-functional teams product managers, designers, data scientists, QA, operations, and compliance to translate business requirements into robust technical solutions, all while adhering to best practices, security standards, and regulatory requirements.
As the technical lead of the Visa Assist AI platform, you will be a hands-on, technically deep, and influential engineer who owns the technical vision and delivery of a multi-agent AI architecture (Visa Assist) serving Visa''s client-facing channels Chat, Email, and Portal. This is a coding-intensive leadership role where you will architect, implement, and ship critical platform components while mentoring engineers, standardizing engineering practices, and aligning with stakeholders to shape the strategic roadmap for Visa''s AI-powered client services.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders and leadership to interpret and translate requirements across the full VisaAssist portfolio spanning inbound channels (Chat, Email, Portal), agent worker routing logic, and platform evolution roadmaps incorporating feedback into technical architecture decisions and working code.
  • Translate business requirements into strategic roadmaps and tactical solutions including routing logic adjustments, guardrail tuning, knowledge base curation, and CRM/billing workflow improvements while escalating potential design issues and downstream dependencies to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Lead system design and architecture, personally architecting and building core infrastructure components: intent classification models, agent routing logic, MCP protocol adapters, and resilience patterns across the distributed multi-agent system.
  • Drive program delivery across the full VisaAssist portfolio intent classification & routing accuracy improvements, agent worker ecosystem (MsgProcessing, CrmDynamics, InvoiceInvestigator, ClientProfile, Transaction Management), MCP protocol adoption and expansion across external services (CRM, Invoice, CAD CP servers), and platform reliability.
  • Write production code daily (60%+ of time), personally implementing the most complex features across the full stack FastAPI endpoints, LangChain agent orchestration, Pydantic v2 schemas, async NATS handlers, and Docker/Kubernetes configurations.
  • Establish and lead engineering standards by implementing reference patterns for the Python / FastAPI / LangChain / Pydantic v2 stack, building shared library modules, and coding MCP server integration adapters (OAuth2 + SSE, mTLS + API Key, REST) that the team adopts as platform-wide standards.
  • Implement LangChain agent patterns including multi-hop MCP and dynamic schema composition; prototype emerging technologies (agentic AI frameworks, MCP protocol evolution, RAG advancements) and recommend technical direction based on hands-on evaluation.
  • Apply advanced debugging techniques to resolve the hardest production issues spanning multiple microservices, NATS messaging, and external service integrations, proactively flagging and addressing systemic risks.
  • Design and implement observability strategies using OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and LangSmith across the full request lifecycle (inbound channel intent worker NATS agent worker external service), with comprehensive distributed tracing and SLA target definitions for each agent worker and external service dependency.
  • Build operational resilience implement NATS messaging failure recovery patterns, manage platform uptime, and drive SLA adherence for Chat/Portal real-time latency, Email throughput, and external service availability.
  • Lead code reviews and enforce coding standards including Pydantic validation patterns, LangChain agent design, async FastAPI endpoints, and security-first practices ensuring quality across the full Python/FastAPI codebase.
  • Partner with cybersecurity teams to address security assessments and implement solutions for findings including API Key Auth, mTLS, OAuth2, PCI-DSS log redaction, and input guardrails (CSAM, injection, SSRF, abuse filtering); teach security-first development practices across the team.
  • Mentor and develop engineers through hands-on pair programming, code reviews, and technical guidance on LangChain agent patterns, MCP protocol implementation, and RAG pipeline optimization; empower team members to own agent worker design and individual microservice delivery.
  • Remain current in skills by continuously evaluating emerging agentic AI frameworks, MCP protocol evolution, and RAG advancements, and investing in team capability growth across the VisaAssist architecture and NATS pub/sub patterns.
  • Forecast labor and support fiscal planning project labor needs for agent worker development, infrastructure capacity, and LLM/GenAI API cost projections; support workforce planning during QBR accounting for platform growth, operational burden, and technical debt reduction.
  • Keep stakeholders and leadership informed of progress across epics, program delivery milestones, and overall platform health for the VisaAssist agent ecosystem.
Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.
Qualifications
Basic Qualifications:
  • 11-15 years'' work experience of work experience with a Bachelor''s Degree or with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters/MBA/JD/MD) or at least 3 years of work experience with a PhD
  • Experience in Java EE technologies, Open-Source frameworks including Spring, React, JavaScript, HTML5, and Web Services (REST/RPC).
  • Experience on microservices, containerization, and ability to quickly build and drive team to support future systems.
  • Experience evaluating business requirements and translating them into technical design documents.
  • Experience in Design Patterns and data modelling.
  • Experience in Kafka and other No-SQL databases.
  • Solid understanding and experience working with Database systems like MySQL and MSSQL.
  • Experience working on application servers like Apache Tomcat, OS platforms like UNIX, Windows, and Linux.
  • Experience with build automation tools including Maven/Gradle/Jenkins/Grunt.
  • Exposure and good knowledge on web application security.
  • Experience in version control tools: BitBucket, Git or similar.

Preferred Qualifications:
  • Programming Languages: Expert-level Python development including async/await architectures, high-performance API design (FastAPI), advanced type systems (Pydantic v2), and serialization optimization (orjson). Ability to set and enforce coding standards across teams.
  • AI/ML Architecture: Deep expertise in LLM integration patterns, agentic AI frameworks (LangChain), RAG pipeline architecture, intent classification systems, and prompt engineering at scale. Experience evaluating and selecting AI models for production use.
  • Protocols & Integration: Expert knowledge of Model Context Protocol (MCP) JSON-RPC 2.0, REST API design, Server-Sent Events (SSE), mTLS, and OAuth2. Experience defining integration standards and protocol strategies across multiple services.
  • Distributed Systems: Extensive experience with event-driven architectures, NATS/Kafka messaging systems, agent-to-agent communication patterns, distributed caching, connection pooling, and failover strategies.
  • API & Platform Architecture: Proven track record of designing and scaling API platforms, defining authentication strategies (OAuth2, API Key, mTLS, X-API-Key), and building resilient microservice ecosystems.
  • Infrastructure & DevOps: Expert knowledge of Kubernetes orchestration strategies, Docker security hardening (non-root, RHEL base), CI/CD pipeline design, and cloud-native deployment patterns.
  • Observability & SRE: Experience designing observability architectures using OpenTelemetry (distributed tracing), Prometheus (metrics/alerting), and LLM-specific tooling (LangSmith). Ability to define SLA frameworks and incident prevention strategies.
  • Security & Compliance: Deep understanding of PCI-DSS compliance requirements, security architecture (mTLS, OAuth2, API Key management), input guardrails design (injection prevention, SSRF, CSAM), and log redaction strategies for sensitive data.
  • SDLC & Engineering Excellence: Experience establishing engineering standards, code quality frameworks (SonarQube), testing strategies, and release management processes across teams.
  • People & Program Leadership: Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers, delegate ownership, drive technical roadmaps, and align with business stakeholders on strategic priorities.
  • Fiscal Planning: Experience with labor forecasting, workforce planning, cost optimization (LLM token usage, infrastructure sizing), and QBR planning processes.
  • GenAI Strategy: Ability to evaluate emerging Generative AI capabilities, recommend model selection and drive adoption of AI-assisted development practices across the organization.
Visa is an EEO Employer
Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

Principal AI Solutions Architect

ABOUT THE ROLE

Five9 is a leading provider of cloud contact center software, bringing the power of Five9 AI and automation to organizations worldwide. The Enterprise-AI Team drives Five9s internal adoption of AI turning emerging capability into real business outcomes across the company.

The Principal AI Solutions Architect is the most senior technical voice on the team and the design authority for Five9s internal AI work the person who turns an approved solution concept into a buildable technical architecture. You partner with the business-facing solutions lead, who owns what a solution must achieve and why; you own how it is built the reference architecture, data and integration design, model / agent / platform selection, security and governance fit, and the technical standards the engineering team builds to. The role demands someone who stays current at all times on the fast-moving AI platform, model, agent, and tooling landscape and on emerging architecture patterns, so every design reflects the best available approach and is sound, secure, and feasible before the build begins.

HOW YOU CONTRIBUTE

  • Technical solution design Translate an approved solution concept into an end-to-end technical architecture components, data flows, integration and API surface, model / agent selection, and non-functional requirements captured as a clear, buildable design.
  • Reference architecture standards Define and maintain the reusable patterns, guardrails, and technical standards the engineering team builds to; keep them current as capabilities and tooling evolve.
  • Platform build-vs-buy strategy Evaluate models, vendors, frameworks, and cloud-platform options; recommend fit, cost, and trade-offs with a clear rationale.
  • Data integration design Design how each solution accesses, moves, and secures company and business data; define the integrations and interfaces the build requires.
  • Security, governance responsible-AI fit Design to information-security, data-classification, and responsible-AI requirements from the start; carry designs through architecture and security review.
  • Design handoff build support Package the technical design to a buildable standard and support the engineering team through implementation as their technical counterpart.
  • Continuous currency Maintain always-current command of the AI platform, model, agent, and tooling landscape and emerging architecture patterns, so every design reflects the best available approach.
  • Technical advisory Advise business partners, engineers, and leadership on feasibility, risk, effort, and sequencing; pressure-test solution designs for technical soundness before they advance.
  • Cross-functional partnership Partner with enterprise architecture, information security, and platform / DevOps teams so designs move cleanly from concept into governed delivery.

SKILLS, COMPETENCIES QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED

  • Bachelors degree (or equivalent experience) in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 12+ years in solution / software / enterprise architecture, ML / AI engineering, or technical solutions / pre-sales engineering including hands-on design of production systems and setting technical direction others build to.
  • Demonstrated ability to design end-to-end technical architectures for AI / ML or data-intensive systems (components, data flows, integrations, non-functionals, and security).
  • Strong command of the modern AI stack LLMs, agent frameworks, retrieval / RAG, orchestration, tool integration, AI-augmented development with a demonstrated habit of staying continuously current.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (Google Cloud preferred) and modern delivery tooling (Git-based version control, CI / CD, infrastructure-as-code).
  • Ability to produce clear, buildable architecture artifacts (reference diagrams, data / integration designs, architecture decision records) and communicate them to both engineers and executives.
  • Working knowledge of security, data-classification, and responsible-AI requirements in an enterprise setting.

SKILLS, COMPETENCIES QUALIFICATIONS PREFERRED

  • Experience in or with contact center / CX technology (Five9 or comparable), or applying AI to CX.
  • Familiarity with responsible-AI, model-risk, and enterprise / solution architecture review practices.
  • Experience defining reusable architecture patterns or platform standards for a delivery team.
  • Prior work at the business / technology boundary in a central enterprise-AI, platform, or transformation function.
  • Cloud (Google Cloud) or enterprise-architecture certifications.

WHERE THIS ROLE SITS

  • Primary focus: technical solution design architecture Owns how every AI solution is built from approved concept to a buildable technical architecture.
  • Works alongside the business solutions lead The business solutions lead owns what a solution must achieve and why; this role owns how it is built.
  • Partners with the engineering team Hands the buildable technical design to the engineers and supports implementation as their technical counterpart.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS

No direct reports (provides technical leadership to the engineering team). Key partners: the business-facing solutions lead the engineering team enterprise architecture information security platform / DevOps. You partner most closely with the business solutions lead on solution design you own the technical design, they own the business design and with the engineers on delivery.

Core AI Engineer Specialist
Experience: 7+ years
Location: Remote

Role Overview
Experience req. can be 7+ years with hands-on work in the pre-transformer era - people who have
built models from scratch before 2017 and not just fine-tuned existing models. Good
understanding of classical ML/DL algorithms and maths behind it.
We value what you have built over where you studied. A GitHub history, a Kaggle record,
merged pull requests to a training library, a paper you reimplemented and evaluated properly —
all of these count for more with us than the name on your degree. If your CV is thin and your
repositories are not, apply anyway. We read the repositories first.

Key Responsibilities
Build models from scratch — architectures, training loops, custom losses, data pipelines
— in PyTorch , not in a wrapper.
Post-train language models: supervised fine-tuning, knowledge distillation under a
real capacity gap, PEFT, and RL from preferences or verifiable rewards.
Implement papers end to end, from an arXiv PDF to working code, and evaluate them
rigorously enough that we can act on the result — including when it is negative.
Adapt general models to specific domains without destroying what they already knew.
Cut GPU cost — parallelism placement, memory, quantisation, serving-time arithmetic
— and measure the saving rather than asserting it.
Track the field and adopt what is worth adopting, quickly, and tell us what is not.

What we require:-
Deep learning fundamentals. Backpropagation, optimisation and transformer
architectures — attention, tokenisation, embeddings — understood mechanically, not as
vocabulary. You should be able to explain why attention is scaled by 1/d, what a
normalisation layer does to gradient flow, and what actually happens in an optimiser step.
Hands-on PyTorch or Keras. You build and train models from scratch — not
fine-tuning through an API, not Trainer with a config file.
LLM post-training, in practice — SFT (data construction, packing, masking, and what
goes wrong); knowledge distillation (forward vs reverse KL, on-policy distillation,
capacity gaps); PEFT ( LoRA and QLoRA , quantisation, adapter placement and rank
selection); RLHF and its descendants — DPO, GRPO, PPO, RLOO : what each
optimises and how each fails.
Engineering. Solid Python . CUDA and GPU-training basics — what is actually
running on the device, and why your step time is what it is. Distributed training (DDP /
FSDP) is a plus, not a requirement.
Proven ability to implement papers end to end — arXiv to working code — and to
evaluate rigorously. Rigorous means seeds, baselines, controls and an honest statement of
the noise floor.
Speed of adoption. This field moves faster than any curriculum. We need people who
read, try, discard and keep the residue — and who can tell the difference between a real
advance and a well-marketed one.

Mandatory Tech Stack:-
Languages: Python, C++, CUDA
Deep Learning: PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy
LLM / Transformers: Hugging Face Transformers, TRL, Tokenizers
Fine-tuning & Post-training: PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA, SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO, RLOO,
Knowledge Distillation
Training: DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, Mixed Precision, Gradient Checkpointing
GPU & Performance: CUDA, NVIDIA GPUs, GPU Profiling, Quantisation, Memory &

We value what you have built over where you studied. A GitHub history, a Kaggle record, merged pull requests to a training library, a paper you reimplemented and evaluated properly — all of these count for more with us than the name on your degree. If your CV is thin and your repositories are not, apply anyway. We read the repositories first.

Key Responsibilities
Build models from scratch — architectures, training loops, custom losses, data pipelines — in PyTorch , not in a wrapper.
Post-train language models: supervised fine-tuning, knowledge distillation under a real capacity gap, PEFT, and RL from preferences or verifiable rewards.
Implement papers end to end, from an arXiv PDF to working code, and evaluate them rigorously enough that we can act on the result — including when it is negative.
Adapt general models to specific domains without destroying what they already knew.
Cut GPU cost — parallelism placement, memory, quantisation, serving-time arithmetic — and measure the saving rather than asserting it.
Track the field and adopt what is worth adopting, quickly, and tell us what is not.

What we require:-
Deep learning fundamentals. Backpropagation, optimisation and transformer architectures — attention, tokenisation, embeddings — understood mechanically, not as vocabulary. You should be able to explain why attention is scaled by 1/d, what a normalisation layer does to gradient flow, and what actually happens in an optimiser step.
Hands-on PyTorch or Keras. You build and train models from scratch — not fine-tuning through an API, not Trainer with a config file.
LLM post-training, in practice — SFT (data construction, packing, masking, and what goes wrong); knowledge distillation (forward vs reverse KL, on-policy distillation, capacity gaps); PEFT ( LoRA and QLoRA , quantisation, adapter placement and rank selection); RLHF and its descendants — DPO, GRPO, PPO, RLOO : what each optimises and how each fails.
Engineering. Solid Python . CUDA and GPU-training basics — what is actually running on the device, and why your step time is what it is. Distributed training (DDP / FSDP) is a plus, not a requirement.
Proven ability to implement papers end to end — arXiv to working code — and to evaluate rigorously. Rigorous means seeds, baselines, controls and an honest statement of the noise floor.
Speed of adoption. This field moves faster than any curriculum. We need people who read, try, discard and keep the residue — and who can tell the difference between a real advance and a well-marketed one.

You will work on complex AI programming problems that require deep engineering judgment across multi-agent orchestration, MCP integrations, secure tool usage, retrieval systems, and cloud deployment.

- You will own the full lifecycle: problem framing, architecture, implementation, deployment, observability, and continuous optimization.

- You will work on hard, real-world AI systems where accuracy, latency, reliability, and governance matter together.

- You will influence engineering quality standards across agent design, LLMOps, and production guardrails while remaining a strong individual contributor.

- Design and implement multi-agent workflows (planner, executor, reviewer, verifier, fallback) with clear control flows and reliability mechanisms.

- Build and integrate MCP-compatible tool ecosystems, including secure access controls, tool permissioning, and auditable execution patterns.

- Architect and optimize RAG pipelines with vector databases, structured retrieval, reranking, and context management.

- Define and enforce output quality standards using schema-driven generation, validation layers, and guardrails.

- Establish evaluation pipelines for correctness, groundedness, robustness, cost, and latency.

- Lead cloud-native deployment and runtime optimization on AWS or Azure, including scalable inference and operational monitoring.

- Drive incident triage and production debugging for agentic workflows.

- Translate business goals into AI system designs with measurable outcomes.

- Mentor junior engineers through design reviews, code reviews, and problem decomposition.


## Must-Have Technical Skills

- 10+ years of software engineering experience with advanced Python expertise.

- Strong command of software design patterns and architecture for complex distributed systems.

- Working depth in deep learning foundations: neural networks, transformers, embeddings, and modern LLM behavior.

- Proven experience building and shipping production agentic AI systems, not only prototypes.

- Proven experience with multi-agent orchestration frameworks and patterns.

- Proven experience implementing MCP server-client integrations in secure enterprise contexts.

- Strong RAG engineering skills with vector databases and retrieval quality tuning.

- Hands-on LLMOps capability: experiment tracking, evaluation frameworks, model monitoring, and release governance.

- Strong prompt, context, and harness engineering capability for high-fidelity outputs.

- Strong understanding of data security and governance controls for AI systems.

- Proficiency in additional programming languages beyond Python.

- Experience with advanced inference optimization (for example multi-GPU sharding, quantization, hardware-specific runtimes).

- Experience with enterprise integration patterns across APIs, data platforms, and workflow systems.

- Experience with financial or document-intelligence style structured extraction systems.

We are hiring an experienced Workday Technical and Functional Consultant to act as the single point of contact between our HR, Finance, IT and business stakeholders and the Workday delivery team. This is a hands-on configuration role, not a program management role: the successful candidate will have spent the last 10 years working inside Workday tenants, configuring solutions, building and troubleshooting integrations, and producing reporting that leaders actually use.
The role sits at the center of demand and delivery. Requests arrive from many directions and in many forms, from a one-line question about an eligibility rule to a multi-quarter programme of work. This person translates those requests into clear problem statements, sizes them honestly, and then distributes the work across the full delivery group, which spans our internal HRIS team members and our Workday consultant. Part of that judgement is deciding at the point of intake which items should sit with the consultant from the start rather than being picked up internally and handed over later. Equally important is the ability to explain the resulting design back to the requesting team in plain business language, and to the delivery group in configuration terms.
Stakeholder Engagement and Requirement Intake
  • Serve as the single point of contact for all stakeholder groups raising Workday demand, running a consistent intake process rather than an ad hoc queue.
  • Gather, challenge and document requirements from HR, Payroll, Finance, IT and business leaders, converting loosely worded asks into precise, testable problem statements.
  • Translate business problem statements into functional and technical design for the team, and translate proposed Workday solutions back into language the requesting team can validate and sign off.
  • Maintain a single prioritized demand backlog, agree sequencing with stakeholders, and communicate trade-offs when capacity is constrained.
  • Run design walkthroughs, impact assessments and readiness sessions ahead of each Workday release.
Configuration and Solution Design
  • Own end-to-end configuration design across the Workday footprint, working hands-on in the tenant rather than directing others from a distance.
  • Configure and troubleshoot business processes, condition rules, security groups, domain and business process security policies, calculated fields and eligibility rules.
  • Assess downstream impact of every change across modules before it is built, and protect tenant hygiene through disciplined use of sandbox, sandbox preview and production migration practices.
  • Define and enforce configuration standards, naming conventions, testing expectations and documentation for the team.
Integrations and Reporting
  • Design, build and support integrations using EIB, Core Connectors, Workday Studio and web services, including error handling, monitoring and re-run procedures.
  • Act as the technical authority on integration issues raised by vendors and downstream system owners, and drive root cause analysis to closure.
  • Build advanced, matrix, composite reporting, and advise stakeholders on the right reporting approach rather than building every request as asked.
  • Ensure reporting and integration outputs respect data privacy, segregation of duties and audit requirements.
Work Sizing, Prioritization and Distribution
  • Assess the complexity, risk and effort of each incoming requirement and assign it to the right owner across the delivery group, which includes internal HRIS team members and our Workday consultant.
  • Balance workload across internal team members and consultant capacity, track progress against commitments, and escalate early when a commitment is at risk.
  • Review the work of internal team members and the consultant, provide technical coaching, and raise the overall configuration capability of the group.
